title: The Kidney and Extracorporeal Therapies in Acute- on- Chronic Liver Failure: What the Nephrologist Needs to Know
one_line_summary: This review summarizes the distinct pathophysiology, diagnostic nuances, medical management, extracorporeal support modalities, and liver-kidney transplantation strategies for acute kidney injury in acute-on-chronic liver failure.
key_pearls: **Acute kidney injury (AKI)** occurs in **30% to >95%** of patients with **acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF)** and carries a **28-day mortality** reaching **50%**.

Unlike decompensated cirrhosis, **AKI** in **ACLF** is heavily driven by **systemic inflammation** and structural damage like **acute tubular necrosis (ATN)** and **bile cast nephropathy (BCN)**, rendering it less responsive to volume expansion and vasopressors.
Post-mortem biopsy studies reveal **bile cast nephropathy (BCN)** in **54%–72.1%** of **ACLF** patients initially diagnosed with **HRS-AKI**, highlighting **significant** clinical underdiagnosis.

Continuous infusion of **terlipressin** (**2–12 mg/day**) combined with **intravenous albumin** (**20–40 g/day**) is preferred over IV boluses due to better tolerability and lower adverse ischemic events.

Hepatic clearance of citrate in **ACLF** is impaired by up to **75%**; while **regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA)** during **CKRT** can be performed, strict monitoring for citrate toxicity (**Ca tot / Ca i ratio >2.5**) is **mandatory**.

Pre-transplant requirement for **kidney replacement therapy (KRT) >30 days** or established **CKD** with **eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73m2** serves as a key criterion for **simultaneous liver-kidney (SLK)** transplantation.

sections.heading: Pathophysiology of AKI in ACLF
sections.content:
- **Systemic Inflammation**: Primary driver of organ failure in **ACLF** initiated by bacterial translocation or infection, causing elevated pathogen-associated molecular patterns (**PAMPs**) and damage-associated molecular patterns (**DAMPs**) that trigger pro-inflammatory cytokine release.
- **Hemodynamic Dysfunction**: Portal hypertension leads to splanchnic vasodilation via nitric oxide, reducing effective arterial blood volume and activating the **renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS)** and sympathetic system, causing intense renal vasoconstriction.
- **Bile Cast Nephropathy (BCN)**: Direct tubular epithelial toxicity and intratubular lumen obstruction from severe hyperbilirubinemia and high urinary bile acids; post-mortem studies demonstrate **BCN** in **54%–72.1%** of **ACLF** patients with **HRS-AKI**.
- **Cardiomyopathy & Paracentesis Dysfunction**: **Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy** (present in up to **60%** of cirrhotics) and **paracentesis-induced circulatory dysfunction (PICD)** (occurring in up to **70%** of **ACLF** patients undergoing modest volume paracentesis without albumin) exacerbate pre-renal hypoperfusion and ischemic **ATN**.
section_pearls: Systemic inflammation is the core driver of structural kidney injury in ACLF.
Bile cast nephropathy is present in >50% of ACLF patients with severe AKI.

sections.heading: Medical Management of AKI in ACLF
sections.content:
- **Initial Resuscitation**: Discontinue diuretics, withdraw nephrotoxic drugs, screen for sepsis, and administer **20%–25% intravenous albumin** at **1 g/kg/day** (maximum **100 g/day**) for **2 days**.
- **Target Mean Arterial Pressure**: Targeting a higher **MAP** of **80–85 mm Hg** in septic shock with cirrhosis improves renal outcomes compared to **60–65 mm Hg**, though **survival** benefit is unproven.
- **Vasopressor Therapy**: **Terlipressin** is the vasoconstrictor of choice, administered via continuous IV infusion (**2–12 mg/day**) combined with **intravenous albumin** (**20–40 g/day**) for up to **14 days**.
- **Early Vasopressor Initiation**: Early initiation of **terlipressin** within **12 h** of non-response to volume expansion yields higher **HRS reversal** (**68.6% vs 31.4%**, **p = 0.03**) and lower **28-day mortality** (**40% vs 65.7%**, **p = 0.031**).
- **Alternative Vasopressors**: Continuous **noradrenaline** infusion is an effective alternative to **terlipressin** for renal perfusion, though **terlipressin** shows non-**significant** numerical superiority in **HRS reversal**.
- **Paracentesis Prophylaxis**: Administer **albumin** at **8 g per liter** of ascitic fluid removed during paracentesis (even for volume **<5 L**) to prevent **PICD** and **AKI**.
section_pearls: Continuous infusion of terlipressin is safer and preferred over IV boluses.
Early terlipressin initiation at 12 hours significantly reduces 28-day mortality.

sections.heading: Kidney Replacement Therapy (KRT) in ACLF
sections.content:
- **Indications**: **Recommended** in **Stage 3 AKI** progressing or non-responsive to vasopressors within **12–24 h**, or for urgent life-threatening uremic/electrolyte complications.
- **Preferred Modality**: **Continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT)** is preferred due to **superior** hemodynamic stability, controlled hyponatremia correction, and lower risk of intracranial hypertension.
- **Anticoagulation Challenges**: High risk of circuit clotting versus severe coagulopathy; **regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA)** is effective but carries risk of citrate accumulation due to a **75% reduction** in hepatic citrate clearance in **ACLF**.
- **Monitoring RCA**: Requires frequent checks of total calcium to ionized calcium ratio (**Ca tot / Ca i > 2.5**) to identify citrate toxicity.
section_pearls: CKRT is the optimal modality to preserve intracranial pressure and hemodynamic stability.
Citrate clearance is reduced by 75% in ACLF; monitor Ca tot / Ca i ratio closely during RCA.

sections.heading: Extracorporeal Liver Support Systems (ELSS)
sections.content:
- **Therapeutic Plasma Exchange (TPE)**: Removes pro-inflammatory cytokines and replaces plasma factors; studies demonstrate improved **30-day and 90-day survival** in non-transplanted **ACLF** patients.
- **Extracorporeal Albumin Dialysis (ECAD)**: Modalities including **MARS**, **SPAD**, and **Prometheus (FPSA)** clear albumin-bound toxins; **MARS** **significantly** lowers **serum creatinine** at **Day 4** (**-20.04% vs -6.43%**).
- **Prometheus (FPSA)**: Subgroup analysis in **Type 1 HRS** demonstrated improved **28-day** (**62% vs 39%**) and **90-day** (**42% vs 6%**) **survival**.
- **Novel Systems**: **DIALIVE** device combines albumin dialysis with hemadsorption; RCT data showed faster **ACLF resolution** (**43% vs 27%**) and improved organ sub-scores (including kidney) at **Day 10**.
- **Double Plasma Molecular Adsorption System (DPMAS)**: Combines resin adsorption with low-volume **TPE**, showing improved **28-day survival** (**97.9% vs 85.4%**) in **HBV-related ACLF**.
section_pearls: ELSS modalities function mainly as a supportive bridge to liver transplantation.
DIALIVE and MARS demonstrate significant capacity for early creatinine reduction.

sections.heading: Liver Transplantation Considerations in ACLF
sections.content:
- **Impact of Pre-transplant AKI**: Pre-transplant renal dysfunction independently predicts post-LT **mortality**; requirement for pre-transplant **KRT** increases **1-year mortality** (HR **2.74**, **95% CI: 1.37–5.51**).
- **Etiology Impact**: Patients with **HRS-AKI** who undergo **LT** achieve post-transplant **survival** comparable to non-AKI patients, whereas patients with **ATN** suffer **significantly** worse **1-year and 5-year survival** and higher rates of **CKD Stage 4/5** (**56% vs 16%**).
- **Simultaneous Liver-Kidney (SLK) Indications**: Indicated for patients requiring **KRT >30 days** or with established pre-transplant **CKD** (**eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73m2**).
- **SLK vs KALT**: **SLK** provides immunological protection to the kidney graft and avoids secondary surgery, showing **superior** recipient and graft **survival** compared to **kidney after liver transplant (KALT)**.
section_pearls: HRS-AKI reverses post-LT, yielding survival similar to patients without pre-LT AKI.
Pre-LT ATN strongly predicts post-transplant persistent CKD Stage 4/5 and mortality.

sections.heading: Areas of Uncertainty and Future Directions
sections.content:
- **Phenotypic Differentiation**: AKI in **ACLF** is less volume-responsive (**21% vs 34%**), features higher structural injury (**32% vs 18%**), and has higher **KRT requirement** (**26% vs 19%**) than in acute decompensation of cirrhosis.
- **Biomarker Utility**: Novel urinary biomarkers like **NGAL** (AUC **0.96** for ATN) and **IL-18** (AUC **0.92**) need standardized cutoff values to reliably differentiate **ATN** from **HRS-AKI**.
- **Trial Limitations & Futility**: Prognostic scoring to determine futility of **KRT** in **LT-ineligible** patients remains poorly validated, necessitating multidisciplinary shared decision-making.
section_pearls: Urinary NGAL shows high diagnostic accuracy (AUC 0.96) for structural ATN in liver failure.
Standardized definitions and AI-driven multimodal prediction models are actively needed.

strengths_limitations:
- Comprehensive synthesis of kidney-liver cross-talk, vasopressor management, and advanced artificial liver support techniques in ACLF.
- Limited by a lack of prospective randomized controlled trial data specifically conducted in ACLF cohorts compared to decompensated cirrhosis.
- Diagnostic criteria rely on observational studies due to the clinical impracticability of kidney biopsies in coagulopathic ACLF patients.

drugs_doses.dose: 1 g/kg/day IV (max 100 g/day) for 2 days for initial expansion; 20-40 g/day alongside vasopressors for up to 14 days; 8 g per liter of ascitic fluid removed during paracentesis
drugs_doses.indication: Volume expansion, prevention of PICD, and co-therapy with vasopressors in HRS-AKI and SBP
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Volume overload, pulmonary edema, and increased risk of lung infections with repeated excessive daily dosing (targeting serum albumin ≥3 g/dL)

drugs_doses.dose: Continuous IV infusion of 2-12 mg/day (or 0.5-2 mg IV every 6 h boluses)
drugs_doses.indication: Hepatorenal syndrome-acute kidney injury (HRS-AKI) in ACLF
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Abdominal pain, diarrhea, intestinal ischemia, peripheral ischemia, myocardial ischemia/angina, and severe respiratory failure

drugs_doses.dose: Continuous IV infusion titrated to target MAP (e.g. MAP >65-85 mm Hg)
drugs_doses.indication: Alternative vasoconstrictor for HRS-AKI and septic shock in ACLF
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Arrhythmias, severe peripheral vasoconstriction, myocardial ischemia

drugs_doses.dose: Infused pre-filter during CKRT, titrated to circuit ionized calcium (0.25–0.35 mmol/L)
drugs_doses.indication: Circuit anticoagulation during continuous kidney replacement therapy in ACLF
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Citrate accumulation/toxicity, systemic hypocalcemia, high total to ionized calcium ratio (>2.5), metabolic acidosis, cardiac arrhythmias, hemodynamic instability
